sentences.text: It’s about getting another vessel’s attention when you need it.
Any vessel may make a light or sound signal to attract attention, as long as it can’t be mistaken for any signal the rules already use.
Or she may direct the beam of her searchlight toward the danger, in a way that doesn’t embarrass any vessel.
Embarrass is an old word here.
It means to dazzle or hamper.
So where do you never point a spotlight?
You’d blind the very person you need to see you.
Shine it at the hazard, or onto your own sails or deck.
And one thing to avoid: high-intensity flashing or revolving lights, such as strobes.
A light used to attract attention also shouldn’t be mistakable for an aid to navigation.
